items.title: Final results of a phase 2 study of the combination of azacitidine and ruxolitinib in patients with myelofibrosis
items.abstract: Final results of a 61-patient phase 2 trial combining azacitidine with the JAK inhibitor ruxolitinib in myelofibrosis, reporting a 72% objective response rate by IWG-MRT criteria and testing whether adding a hypomethylating agent to JAK inhibition modifies disease beyond spleen and symptom control.

items.title: Inhibition of nucleoporin 214 depletes leukemia stem cells by promoting heme catabolism and lipid peroxidation
items.abstract: Preclinical study identifying NUP214 as an overexpressed fitness determinant that sustains AML leukemia stem cells by restricting heme catabolism and suppressing ferroptosis; a selective NUP214 degrader (0449-b) triggers stem-cell ferroptosis and antileukemic activity while sparing normal hematopoietic stem cells.

items.title: Cheminformatic identification of small molecules targeting acute myeloid leukemia
items.abstract: Cheminformatic screen of ~4.2 million compounds identifying small molecules that selectively kill AML cells through combined apoptotic agonism, autophagic induction and glutathione-reductase inhibition, with strong synergy alongside midostaurin and venetoclax in patient-derived cells.

items.title: Impact of cytoreductive therapy in myeloproliferative neoplasm-associated splanchnic vein thrombosis
items.abstract: International GASTRO-MPN cohort of 757 MPN patients with splanchnic vein thrombosis, using time-dependent modeling to show cytoreductive therapy was associated with reduced recurrent thrombosis (HR 0.67), driven by fewer splanchnic-bed extensions/recurrences.

items.title: Prognostic factors and survival outcomes in relapsed/refractory aggressive B-cell lymphomas treated with epcoritamab
items.abstract: Real-world analysis of 157 patients with relapsed/refractory aggressive B-cell lymphoma treated with the CD3xCD20 bispecific epcoritamab outside trials (ORR 49.6%, CRR 31.9%), finding ECOG >=2, elevated LDH and prior-line refractoriness predicted inferior survival, with higher grade >=3 CRS than pivotal trials.

items.title: Daratumumab in transplant-ineligible or -deferred newly diagnosed multiple myeloma: minimal residual disease in CEPHEUS
items.abstract: Expanded MRD analysis of the phase 3 CEPHEUS trial showing quadruplet daratumumab-VRd raised overall MRD-negativity versus VRd (60.9% vs 39.4% at 10^-5) with higher sustained negativity and improved progression-free survival, establishing D-VRd as a new standard of care for transplant-ineligible or -deferred newly diagnosed myeloma.

items.title: Mezigdomide reverses T-cell exhaustion through degradation of IKZF1/IKZF3 and reinvigoration of cytokine production pathways
items.abstract: Mechanistic study showing the cereblon modulator mezigdomide degrades IKZF1/IKZF3 to reverse T-cell exhaustion, restore proinflammatory cytokine production and enhance killing by the BCMA T-cell engager alnuctamab, supporting combination of mezigdomide with bispecifics in multiple myeloma.

items.title: Ibrutinib for early-stage CLL: genetic risk factors and treatment outcome in the GCLLSG CLL12 trial
items.abstract: Genetic-subgroup analysis of the randomized CLL12 trial of ibrutinib versus placebo in asymptomatic early-stage CLL, finding ibrutinib improved event-free survival across most high-risk subgroups but not del(17p)/TP53-mutated disease and conferred no overall-survival benefit, reaffirming watch-and-wait as standard of care.

items.title: High-risk single-refractory and double-refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia: feasibility and impact of alloHCT
items.abstract: Study of 47 high-risk CLL patients showing double-refractory disease (to both covalent BTK and BCL2 inhibitors) carried a dismal 21-month median overall survival; allogeneic transplantation was feasible (2-year OS 67%) but exploratory comparisons did not demonstrate a clear survival benefit over non-transplant.

items.title: Modulation of the bone marrow microenvironment by acute B-cell lymphoblastic leukemia-derived large oncosomes
items.abstract: Preclinical work showing BCR-ABL1-positive B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells release large oncosomes that reprogram mesenchymal stromal cells toward a tumor-supportive, adipocyte-primed phenotype by modulating IGF1 availability, revealing an extracellular-vesicle communication route as a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: Tisa-cel and axi-cel CAR structure influences the development of resistance to CD19-CAR-T therapy
items.abstract: Experimental study showing CAR costimulatory architecture governs antigen escape: repeated exposure to 4-1BB-based (tisa-cel-like) CD19 CAR-T cells drove FMC63-epitope and total CD19 loss with resistance-associated mutations, whereas CD28-based (axi-cel-like) CARs did not, suggesting design choices that could reduce relapse.

items.title: Adaptive bridging and holding therapy frequently reduces tumor burden and is associated with reduced toxicity after CAR-T cell therapy in multiple myeloma
items.abstract: Single-center analysis of 88 relapsed/refractory myeloma patients receiving BCMA CAR-T, finding deeper pre-infusion response (>=VGPR) was associated with roughly halved grade >=2 toxicity, identifying response-adapted holding and bridging therapy as a modifiable determinant of CAR-T safety.

items.title: Allogeneic stem cell transplantation after myeloablative conditioning with fludarabine, thiotepa, and cyclophosphamide in relapsed or refractory aggressive B-cell and T-cell lymphomas: results of the prospective ASTRAL study
items.abstract: Prospective multicenter ASTRAL trial of myeloablative fludarabine/thiotepa/cyclophosphamide conditioning before allogeneic transplant in 60 patients with relapsed/refractory aggressive B- or T-cell lymphoma; the 1-year PFS primary endpoint was not met, but transplantation was effective after CAR-T failure and showed a strong graft-versus-lymphoma effect in T-cell lymphoma.

items.title: Inhibiting thromboinflammation via interleukin-4 binding to platelet glycoprotein VI and suppression of thrombosis
items.abstract: Basic study showing the anti-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-4 binds platelet glycoprotein VI to suppress collagen signaling, aggregation and both arterial and venous thrombosis, and that a GPVI-derived interfering peptide reverses this - nominating the IL-4-GPVI axis as a target for thrombotic disorders.

items.title: Histidine-rich glycoprotein modulates platelet adhesion and aggregation by binding to GPIbalpha and GPIIb/IIIa
items.abstract: Study demonstrating histidine-rich glycoprotein competes with von Willebrand factor and fibrinogen at platelet GPIbalpha and GPIIb/IIIa to attenuate adhesion, aggregation and thrombus growth; reduced plasma HRG in sepsis and COVID-19 produced a hyperreactive platelet phenotype, linking HRG to both coagulation and platelet biology.

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of iron deficiency screening in pregnancy across ferritin-based thresholds
items.abstract: First US cost-effectiveness analysis of ferritin-based iron-deficiency screening in pregnancy, finding screening at a 30 ug/L threshold was the preferred strategy across all analyses (ICER ~$34,000/QALY versus no screening) and supporting routine second- and third-trimester screening.

items.title: Perioperative durvalumab for resectable non-small cell lung cancer: updated outcomes from the phase 3 AEGEAN trial
items.abstract: Updated phase 3 AEGEAN results showing perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy sustained an event-free survival benefit (HR 0.69) with numerical improvements in disease-free and overall survival versus chemotherapy alone in resectable NSCLC, supporting it as a treatment option.

items.title: Long-term survival outcomes of modified-FOLFOXIRI plus cetuximab versus bevacizumab in RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer: final analysis of the DEEPER trial
items.abstract: Final analysis of the randomized phase 2 DEEPER trial in RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer, finding that in RAS/BRAF wild-type left-sided tumors modified-FOLFOXIRI plus cetuximab prolonged progression-free survival (14.8 vs 11.9 months) and overall survival (50.2 vs 40.2 months) versus bevacizumab.

items.title: Adjuvant pembrolizumab for the treatment of clear cell renal cell carcinoma: five-year results from the phase 3 KEYNOTE-564 study
items.abstract: Fourth interim analysis of the phase 3 KEYNOTE-564 trial at a median 70-month follow-up, showing adjuvant pembrolizumab sustained disease-free (HR 0.71) and overall survival (HR 0.66) benefits over placebo in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma at increased risk of recurrence.

items.title: Belzutifan plus lenvatinib versus cabozantinib in patients with previously treated advanced renal cell carcinoma (LITESPARK-011): a phase 3 trial
items.abstract: Open-label phase 3 LITESPARK-011 trial in 747 patients with advanced clear-cell renal cell carcinoma progressing after checkpoint therapy, showing the HIF-2alpha inhibitor belzutifan plus lenvatinib prolonged progression-free survival (14.8 vs 10.7 months) versus cabozantinib without a significant overall-survival difference.

items.title: Systemic therapy considerations in older adults with early-stage breast cancer: a review
items.abstract: Review of systemic therapy for older adults with early-stage breast cancer, weighing recurrence risk against treatment toxicity across subtypes and covering adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors, neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in triple-negative disease, and tools to avoid both over- and under-treatment.

items.title: Functional role of skull lymphoid structures in CNS immunosurveillance
items.abstract: Study identifying germinal-center-like lymphoid structures within skull bone marrow, containing follicular-helper-like T cells that drive B-cell activation and humoral immunity, that surveil CNS-derived antigens and contribute to anti-tumor immune responses in mouse brain-cancer models.

items.title: Synthetic transcription factors designed by domain recombination enhance CAR T cell antitumor function
items.abstract: Study assembling novel synthetic AP-1 transcription factors from recombined protein domains (DESynR) that reprogram human CAR T cells into non-natural states optimizing effector function, cytotoxicity and persistence, outperforming natural AP-1 factors across in vitro and in vivo antitumor assays.

items.title: Rewiring immunity with in vivo CAR T cell engineering
items.abstract: Perspective on generating CAR T cells directly within the patient to bypass the manufacturing complexity and access barriers of ex vivo therapy, outlining lymphocyte-targeting principles, pharmacology and biodistribution, emerging safety issues and the path to clinical implementation.

items.title: RAD51 stabilizes neutrophil extracellular traps to compartmentalize inflammation
items.abstract: Study showing the DNA-recombination protein RAD51 branches and structurally stabilizes neutrophil extracellular traps to compartmentalize inflammation; RAD51 inhibition destabilized NETs and paradoxically released NET components that drove IL-6 production and worsened systemic type 2 inflammation, linking DNA repair to innate immunity.
